picks.title: Disney Partners With Adobe On AI Tools That Turn Artists' Sketches Into Finished Concept Art
picks.rationale: Biggest studio-tool deal of the week (Adobe as Disney's official AI innovation partner, bespoke Firefly Foundry models on Disney IP); Cartoon Brew's version carries the concrete artist workflow (sketch to rendered concept art). Kept over the Variety report (same cluster c0).
picks.excerpt: Under the multiyear alliance Adobe gives Disney Firefly, Firefly Foundry, Premiere, Photoshop and dedicated engineers to build bespoke AI models trained on Disney IP, including tools that turn hand-drawn sketches into fully rendered concept art.

picks.title: Framestore Brings Hybrid AI/VFX to Sky's Christmas Campaign
picks.rationale: Practical VFX-house case study: where Framestore slotted AI (previs, character removal, self-animating costumes) inside a traditional CG pipeline on a Dave Meyers spot.
picks.excerpt: Framestore built AI tools into its traditional VFX pipeline for Sky's 'That's Christmas Sorted' spot directed by Dave Meyers, using them for previs, character removal and self-animating costumes alongside CG environments.

picks.title: Real-Time Video at Batch Size One
picks.rationale: Primary-source technical release from Runway on serving a ~57B autoregressive video model in real time (24 fps, 166.7ms chunks) for Characters; distinct from the earlier Summit safety talk.
picks.excerpt: Runway details how it serves its ~57B-parameter autoregressive video diffusion model in real time for Characters: a new four-frame chunk every 166.7ms at 24 fps per user, running one session across four H100s.

picks.title: Original 'Return of the Living Dead' Stars Slam AI-Generated Sequel
picks.rationale: New concrete event: an almost entirely AI-generated sequel to a cult horror IP shipped Oct. 31 using original cast likenesses without filming, and the stars publicly disown it; a fresh likeness-consent flashpoint not covered in movies' 30-day history.
picks.excerpt: 'Return of the Living Dead: Aftermath', released Oct. 31 by DragonFLIX, is almost entirely AI-generated imagery and dialogue; original stars Linnea Quigley and Beverly Randolph say they appear without having filmed anything and disown it.

picks.title: AI Could Make Films Costlier Than the 35mm Era, Korean Pioneers Warn
picks.rationale: Hard production-cost numbers from working AI-feature makers at TCCF (token bill over KRW500M / $366K for a 100-minute feature, revisions as paid re-renders multiplying cost up to tenfold) that cut against the 'AI is cheap' pitch; distinct from the 11-08 Core Studio TCCF launch card.
picks.excerpt: At TCCF in Taipei, Studio Meta-K CEO Kim Kwang-jib said the token bill alone for a 100-minute AI feature can top KRW500 million ($366,000) with top commercial tools, and that every revision is a paid re-render, so piecemeal client notes can multiply costs tenfold. He and MBC C&I's Lee Sang-wook, whose AI feature 'Raphael' heads to Korean cinemas, also covered hybrid shoots and new crew roles.
